scenes.headline: What a merged kernel change does and does not leak
scenes.sub: A dense Qwen4-27B, read against the code.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Scarf! A post says a merged kernel change leaks a dense Qwen four model. Let's see what the code really shows.

scenes.text: The pull request is real, but it says far less than the post claims, and the architecture it points at is already public.
scenes.say: The change is real, but it says far less than the post claims. And the architecture it points at is already public.

steps.say: The screenshot names two per-rank shapes: Q twelve over K V two, and a hidden width of five thousand one hundred and twenty.
Both match the released twenty-seven-billion model: twenty-four query heads over four K V heads.
What the dense model adds is already public in vLLM.

scenes.title: The dense model, as far as it can be read

steps.say: A token climbs three Gated DeltaNet layers, then one sparse attention layer, repeated, with a dense feed-forward block.
Beside every layer run residual lanes. Four is Flash-Next's count, so for the dense model it is reasoned.
The sparse layer compresses keys into blocks of four, and reads only two thousand and forty-eight tokens.

steps.label: Dense: every key
steps.say: Dense attention reads every earlier key. At two hundred and sixty-two thousand tokens, that is seventeen gigabytes a step.

steps.label: Blocks of 4 keys
steps.say: Sparse attention first compresses keys into blocks of four, and scores them.

steps.label: Top blocks only
steps.say: It keeps the best blocks. The read stays near two thousand tokens.

scenes.title: The decode ceiling
scenes.text: tok/s = bandwidth / bytes streamed per step

parts.note: 456 GB/s on one card, as published
parts.say: Bandwidth is the card's memory speed.
Each step streams the weights once.

scenes.say: Decoding one stream is bound by memory.

scenes.title: Ceilings, tokens per second
scenes.note: ceilings before any speed-up from drafting
scenes.say: Reasoned ceilings: about thirty tokens a second on one card at INT4, and sixty on two.

scenes.text: A kernel pull request proves kernels exist. The shapes are inference, and the release is unconfirmed.
scenes.say: A kernel change proves kernels exist. The shapes are inference, and the release is unconfirmed.

recap: The pull request is real, a screenshot only
Shapes carried over from the released 27B
scenes.say: To recap: a real change, shapes carried over, and no release.
